facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of a rapidly enlarging left breast mass
no history of pain, trauma, fever, anorexia, or weight loss
the left breast had a 20 cm × 20 cm well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump
the right breast was normal
the mass was not fixed to skin or underlying muscle
the overlying skin was tense and shiny with prominent superficial veins
no nipple discharge and no axillary lymphadenopathy
routine hematological and biochemical tests, including ESR, were within normal limits
a chest radiograph was normal
ultrasonography of the left breast revealed a heterogeneous parenchymal pattern suggestive of fibroadenoma
fine-needle aspiration cytology of the lump showed pathology suggesting fibroadenoma
she was premenarcheal

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a rapidly enlarging, well-circumscribed, firm, and mobile breast lump, combined with ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration cytology results suggestive of fibroadenoma, supports this diagnosis.
Although less likely than fibroadenoma, the large size and rapid growth of the breast mass could also be consistent with a phyllodes tumor, which can present similarly.
The well-circumscribed and mobile nature of the breast lump could also suggest a breast hamartoma, although this is less common and the imaging findings are not as typical for this condition.

rationales.F01: Rapidly enlarging breast mass is concerning but not specific to fibroadenoma.
rationales.F03: A well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump is highly suggestive of fibroadenoma.
rationales.F05: The mass not being fixed to skin or underlying muscle leans towards a benign process like fibroadenoma.
rationales.F06: Tense and shiny skin with prominent superficial veins could indicate a more aggressive tumor like phyllodes tumor.
rationales.F10: Ultrasonography findings are highly suggestive of fibroadenoma.
rationales.F11: Fine-needle aspiration cytology results strongly support the diagnosis of fibroadenoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration cytology findings suggest fibroadenoma, which aligns with the clinical presentation of a well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, mobile lump.
